extracted.intended_audience: individual investigators preparing an application to the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and review criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1 Clinical Trial Optional), including required Essay content, eligibility, submission constraints, and the peer review criteria emphasizing innovativeness, investigator qualities, and change in research direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pioneer Award purpose and pioneering requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Director’s Pioneer Award Program supports individual scientists of exceptional creativity who propose highly innovative research projects with the potential to produce a major impact on broad, important areas relevant to the mission of NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered pioneering, the proposed research must reflect substantially different scientific directions from those already being pursued in the investigator’s research program or elsewhere. The proposed project must reflect a fundamental new insight which may involve exceptionally innovative approaches and/or radically unconventional hypotheses. Applications for projects that are straightforward extensions of ongoing research should not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis in review (three emphases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will emphasize: (1) The significance and innovation of the proposed project; (2) The investigator's evidence for past innovation and the ability to commit effort that is sufficient for the proposed project; (3) A change in research direction that is not a logical extension or scale-up of ongoing efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Pioneer Award applications do not require preliminary data, specific aims, or a detailed research plan, reviewers focus on these emphases to judge pioneering potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in research direction
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in research direction is considered to be one that is not a logical extension or scale-up of ongoing efforts, but rather one that is motivated by a fundamental new insight that prompts a new line of research or a substantial departure from an existing line of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the new direction may build on prior work as a foundation, it cannot be an obvious extension or scale-up of the investigator's current research program; it must reflect a fundamental new insight and may involve radically unconventional hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator evidence of innovativeness and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate evidence of exceptional creativity and past innovation, and show they have the skills, knowledge, and resources to carry out the proposed pioneering research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Essay should provide concrete evidence of innovativeness (e.g., ability to integrate diverse information, question paradigms, persist through failure, collaborate across disciplines, and the energy/concentration to plan and execute strategies). Letters of reference (three required) should also describe the applicant’s qualities that support claims to scientific innovativeness and creativity with specific examples when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required research effort commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pioneer awardees are required to commit the major portion (more than 6 person-months or at least 51%) to activities supported by the Pioneer Award research project in the first three years of the project period. Effort may be reduced to a minimum of 4 person-months (33%) in year four and 3 person-months (25%) in year five.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effort toward teaching, administrative, or clinical duties should not be included. Applicants with current research commitments equal to 6 person-months or more must adjust existing commitments or should not submit if they cannot meet the requirement. Include a Statement of research effort commitment in the Essay describing how required effort will be met/adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preliminary data or detailed experimental plans required
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary data and detailed experimental plans are not requested and should not be provided as part of the Pioneer Award application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project description should not provide a detailed experimental plan but must give reviewers a clear sense of the overall research to be pursued and convince them that the research will be pursued in a robust and rigorous manner. Prominently indicate that neither a detailed plan nor extensive preliminary data are being provided per the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay required and required Essay sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy: Attach the Essay (pdf named 'Essay.pdf') containing specific sections in the order given with the headings shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required sections (in order): Scientific Areas (1-digit codes and abbreviations for primary and secondary at beginning of essay), Project Title, Project description (scientific challenge/opportunity, importance, pioneering approaches, and prominence that detailed plans/preliminary data are not provided), Evidence of PD/PI's innovativeness, How the planned research differs from PD/PI's past or current work, Suitability for Pioneer Award program, Statement of research effort commitment. References and figures may be included but must fit within the page limit. Letters of collaboration will not be accepted; collaborator names/affiliations may be listed in the PHS Assignment Request Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Area Designations (assignment aid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must designate two scientific areas (a primary and secondary) by entering the one-digit code and abbreviation (e.g., '1 BSS') and include them at the beginning of the Essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the primary and secondary science areas most appropriate for the proposed project; this helps assign applications to reviewers. Enter primary first followed by a semicolon and secondary. Also include the same designations in the Agency Routing Identifier Field. Example: '1 BSS; 7 NS'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirement and referee instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must arrange to have three (and only three) letters of reference submitted on their behalf. Letters must be submitted via the specified eRA Commons link by 5:00 p.m. (local time of the referee) on the application due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters are confidential; applicants will not have access. In two pages or less, referees should describe the applicant’s qualities supporting claims to innovativeness and likelihood to conduct groundbreaking research, with specific examples when possible. Referees do not need eRA Commons accounts but must enter the applicant’s eRA Commons User ID and exact last name. Late letters will not be accepted and applications with fewer than three letters will not be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PD/PI only and limits on PD/PI submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only single PD/PI applications are allowed; applications with multiple PD(s)/PI(s) will not be accepted. Individuals may serve as the PD/PI on only one application (see Section III.3.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications must be submitted as new applications regardless of previous submissions to the program. No reference to prior applications may be included; any reference may be grounds for administrative withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicant organizations and foreign ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible organizations include a broad set of domestic institutions (institutions of higher education, nonprofits, for-profits, governments, small businesses, etc.). Non-domestic (non-U.S.) entities are not eligible to apply as applicant organizations; non-domestic components of U.S. organizations are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign components (as defined in the NIH Grants Policy Statement) are allowed, but foreign institutions cannot be the applicant organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and project period constraints and budget entry instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will be for $700,000 in direct costs per year plus applicable F&A costs for a project period limited to five years. Total five-year direct cost should be entered as $3,500,000 in the SF424 fields 'Total Federal Funds Requested' and 'Total Federal & Non-Federal Funds'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A detailed budget and other budget forms are not requested and will not be accepted. Applicable F&A costs will be determined at award and should not be included in the budget request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form and format restrictions (fields not used)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several standard application components are modified or prohibited for this FOA: Specific Aims DO NOT USE; Bibliography & References Cited DO NOT USE (references may be included within the Essay page limit if essential); Equipment DO NOT USE; Other Attachments DO NOT USE; Profile Senior Key Person 1 DO NOT USE; Additional Biographical Sketch(es) DO NOT USE; Letters of Support DO NOT USE; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements DO NOT USE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities & Other Resources statement: 1 page maximum. Only the PD/PI may serve as senior/key personnel and submit a Biographical Sketch. Limited Appendix materials allowed per Application Guide. Resource Sharing Plans expected as Just-in-Time if award is being considered. Provide names and affiliations of collaborators in PHS Assignment Request Form rather than letters of collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criterion: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials, reviewers should assess whether the scientific rationale and need are well supported by clinical/preclinical studies or mechanisms, and whether the trial is necessary to test safety/efficacy/effectiveness that could change clinical practice, community behaviors, or health policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, taking into consideration the review criteria and additional review criteria as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major scientific impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects and Inclusion considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will evaluate the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, and inclusion of individuals of all ages to determine if it is justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information on review of the Inclusion section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals review criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals based on: (1) description of proposed procedures (species, strains, ages, sex, numbers); (2) justification for use of animals vs alternatives and appropriateness of species; (3) interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain and injury; (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess use of chimpanzees as they would any other application proposing vertebrate animals. See the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards review consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If needed, reviewers will determine whether adequate protections are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent research and biosafety considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For Select Agent research, reviewers will assess (1) Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) registration status of entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer, and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all required information in the application for projects involving Select Agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects involving key biological and/or chemical resources, reviewers will comment on brief plans proposed for identifying and ensuring the validity of those resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise authentication plans when relevant; reviewers will treat this as an additional review consideration (not scored separately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and period of support review consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although a detailed budget is not submitted, reviewers will still assess reasonableness of the requested total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview stage for top candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the review criteria stated, candidates identified as most outstanding will be invited to Bethesda, MD for interviews in April 2021. Interviews will be conducted by a panel of outside experts using the same review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected candidates will receive written critiques and will not be allowed to appeal initial peer review. Final funding decisions consider review outcomes plus program priorities and funds availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness, compliance, and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, applications will be evaluated for completeness and compliance with application instructions by the Center for Scientific Review and for responsiveness by components of participating organizations; incomplete, non-compliant and/or non-responsive applications will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformance to all requirements in the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide and the FOA is required and strictly enforced. Applicants are encouraged to apply early to allow time to correct errors identified during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on resubmissions/renewals/revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmissions, renewals, and revisions are not applicable for this FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications must be new (A0). Appeals of initial peer review will not be accepted for applications submitted in response to this FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection considerations beyond peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Following peer review, funding decisions by Council will consider: scientific & technical merit, availability of funds, and relevance of the project to program priorities (including potential to lead groundbreaking, cross-cutting science; scientific balance in the portfolio; potential to invigorate exceptionally innovative and impactful science; and conformance to clinical trial policies of administering IC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff will weigh portfolio balance and programmatic priorities in addition to peer review scores when making funding recommendations.
